title: Disable recovery monitor before recovery start

timeline.message:
Disable recovery monitor before recovery start

We do nontrivial amounts of work before we start a peer recovery,
particularly recovering from the local translog up to its global
checkpoint. Today the recovery monitor is running during this time, and
will (repeatedly) fail the recovery if it takes more than 30 minutes to
complete. With this commit we disable the recovery monitor until this
local process has completed.

Closes #93542
timeline.author: David Turner

timeline.body: Hi @DaveCTurner, I've created a changelog YAML for you.

I don't see a great way to test this change unfortunately, at least not without introducing a whole lot of other changes, and I am not even sure this feature should exist any more so I don't think it's a good use of time to build out a test suite now. I opened https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/93544 to track this debt.
Kind of unrelated to your change, but I find the name `failureHandler` a bit confusing. Isn't this also called when the pre-recovery step completes successfully?

reply.body: Yeah I also don't 100% like this name, but nor can I think of a better one. The point is that this listener _only_ handles failures (i.e. it's a no-op on success, apart from releasing things that need releasing) and therefore needs further modification (i.e. a `.map()`) before it can be used as a proper listener.

timeline.body: Just a question for my learning: does this mean also when the preRecovery call fails, we would disable the recovery monitor? If yes, I guess that is unnecessary but harmless since the peer recover has failed?

reply.body: Closing the releasable means we _re-enable_ the monitor. But yes this doesn't really do anything, the recovery is already dead at this point.

timeline.body: I encountered a test failure that seems to have been introduced by this change so I reverted it. I'll investigate further and open another PR shortly.
